title: perf-bench-scratch-isaac-chen-2026-03-10
content:
Objective:
- Quick scratchpad for latency/throughput runs on 13B model variants and quantization profiles. Capture commands, numbers, and immediate hypotheses. Not a polished report.

Environment / test harness:
- infra: aws-us-west-2, a100-80gb instances for baseline (p4d-like), then a100-40gb and g5 for cost checks.
- harness: internal loadtester v0.9 (python script: perf/run_load_test.py), tokenized with tiktoken-like encoder.
- model artifacts tested: llama-2-13b-chat (hf export), llama-2-13b-quant-8bit, llama-2-13b-quant-4bit (GPTQ). Also a smaller baseline: mosaic-7b-8bit.
- runtime flags: --batch-size, --max-concurrency, --kv-cache-enabled, --kv-cache-size=4GB, --stream=false, --seq-len=2048 (default), --prefill-parallel=true.

Key commands used (local harness):
- baseline: python perf/run_load_test.py --model llama-2-13b-chat --instance a100-80 --batch-size 1 --concurrency 1 --seq 512 --duration 300
- batched: python perf/run_load_test.py --model llama-2-13b-chat --batch-size 4 --concurrency 8 --seq 512 --duration 300
- quant: python perf/run_load_test.py --model llama-2-13b-quant-8bit --batch-size 4 --concurrency 12 --seq 512 --duration 300 --kv-cache-enabled

Observed metrics (p50/p95 latencies in ms, throughput in tokens/s):
1) llama-2-13b-chat (fp16), a100-80, batch=1, concurrency=1, seq=512:
   - p50: 210 ms, p95: 420 ms, tokens/s: 1200
   - notes: stable, but high cost per token. Prefill dominates for long contexts.
2) llama-2-13b-chat, a100-80, batch=4, concurrency=8:
   - p50: 360 ms, p95: 780 ms, tokens/s: 5200
   - notes: batching increases throughput ~4.3x but tail latency worsens (p95 > 2x).
3) llama-2-13b-quant-8bit, a100-40, batch=4, concurrency=12, kv-cache enabled:
   - p50: 280 ms, p95: 560 ms, tokens/s: 4800
   - notes: 8-bit quant gives ~10-15% throughput drop vs fp16 on a100-80 but lowers memory footprint allowing higher concurrency. KV-cache hits (local synthetic session pattern) improved median by ~30%.
4) llama-2-13b-quant-4bit (gptq), a100-40, batch=8, concurrency=16:
   - p50: 310 ms, p95: 690 ms, tokens/s: 6200
   - notes: 4-bit (GPQT) increases throughput w/ same memory but higher compute overhead per token — decent win for throughput but tail latency still problematic at high concurrency.
5) mosaic-7b-8bit baseline, a100-40, batch=8, concurrency=20:
   - p50: 110 ms, p95: 240 ms, tokens/s: 7200
   - notes: much lower latency/ cost. Good option for lightweight workloads.

KV-cache micro-observations:
- With realistic session traffic (prefix reuse ~40%), KV-cache hit rate around 35-45% in our synthetic probe.
- Cache warmup reduces prefill cost by up to ~40% for repeated prompts.
- Eviction policy: LRU with size 4GB seems fine for 2–3k active sessions, but needs tuning for higher multiplexer workloads.

Batching behavior:
- Continuous batching implementation (our runtime) increases throughput predictably but queuing increases p95 nonlinearly with concurrency spikes.
- For SLOs targeting p95 < 500ms, effective max batch size for 13B is 4 on a100-80 in our tests. Larger batch sizes require stricter queuing controls or preemptive prioritization.

Quick hypotheses / takeaways:
- 8-bit quantization gives the best cost-memory tradeoff for Dedicated pools where we trade a small throughput loss for denser packing.
- 4-bit GPQT is promising for throughput-oriented tiers but requires more careful tail-latency mitigation (dynamic batching limits or priority lanes).
- KV-cache is a high ROI feature for chat-heavy workloads — even moderate hit rates materially reduce token cost and median latency.
- For low-latency interactive products, prefer smaller models (7B) or reserved single-concurrency nodes; for high throughput async workloads, favor 4-bit-packed 13B with aggressive batching.

Open questions / next runs:
- Re-run with streaming=true to measure end-to-end first-byte latency vs full-response latency.
- Test different eviction policies (LRU vs segmented) under heavy session churn.
- Try prefill-parallel=false to see impact on p95 for long seqs (512+).
- Run cost model (tokens/s * instance-hour) to estimate per-token cost across fp16/8bit/4bit for committed vs hosted scenarios.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add script to auto-plot p50/p95 vs concurrency and batch-size (simple matplotlib script).
- Post initial findings to RFC channel and link PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/789 (drafted changes to batching heuristics).
- Share select graphs with Maya and Jordan; ask Maya to run same 4-bit GPQT jobs on g5 for cross-hardware comparison.

Raw logs location (local): /mnt/perf_logs/isaac/2026-03-10/ (zipped outputs + CSV).

Rough immediate recommendation for Dedicated trial config:
- 13B quant-8bit pool, instance a100-40, default batch-size 4, max-concurrency per-gpu 12, KV-cache enabled, SLO target p95 < 600ms.

End of scratchpad.

(unfinished — leaving here so Maya/Jordan can pick up and iterate)
